title: Volume 1 Chapter 7: I Don't Understand Love 1
content: As I passed in front of the training grounds after finishing Lady Rana's examination, I caught sight of Krush swinging her sword alone.
With a sword in one hand and a shield in the other, her movements were precise and devoid of waste.
However, her face bore a somewhat grim expression, even hinting at anxiety.
I felt a sense of discomfort at her appearance.
"Is Krush always like that?"
I couldn't help but ask May, who was standing beside me. She was also watching Krush's demeanor.
"Yes, she is! Lady Krush always trains alone."
May's voice lacked its usual brightness, and she wore a somewhat lonely expression.
"Why is she alone? As the vice-captain, shouldn't she have more time to train with the other members?"
May looked a bit troubled by my question, choosing her words carefully as she began to explain.
Lady Krush is of no attribute.
That's why she can't use magic.
While others use magic in combat, Lady Krush can't do that, so she trains by herself.
I was a bit surprised. No attribute, huh?
In this world, there are few who cannot use magic.
As a vice-captain of the Knight Order, one would generally possess some attribute and be able to use at least one or two spells.
However, no attribute, while rare like the holy attribute, is not welcomed.
It is said that those of no attribute cannot cast any spells at all.
"I see... So that's why she's training so hard."
That was common knowledge in many places, yet it felt absurd to me.
Yes, that's right.
Lady Krush can't use magic, so she has honed her sword and shield skills more than anyone else.
In terms of fighting with a one-handed sword and shield, she's the strongest in the order!
May spoke proudly, but her tone also conveyed respect for Krush, along with a hint of concern.
"But is it really okay for Krush? It feels lonely that she trains alone, worrying about being of no attribute."
I couldn't help but voice my thoughts. I was deeply concerned about her.
I could only imagine how lonely she must have felt, forced to fight alone because of her lack of attribute.
Lady Krush is a strong person.
That's why she never shows weakness to anyone about being of no attribute.
But I know.
I know how she truly feels...
May's voice grew a little quieter. I turned to look at her.
In her eyes, there was kindness, but also a hint of sadness.
Lady Krush is always troubled about whether she is worthy of being the vice-captain.
Because she has no attribute, she doesn't want to burden anyone...
That's why she thinks she must become stronger than anyone else and swings her sword desperately.
Her words tightened my chest. I felt like I understood a little of why Krush continued to fight in solitude.
"Is she really troubled as vice-captain? Doesn't everyone recognize her?"
Even as I said this, I still couldn't find an answer to how to help Krush with her loneliness.
Of course, everyone respects Lady Krush!
Even though she can't use magic because she has no attribute, her efforts are genuine, and many members have had their lives saved by her.
But Lady Krush herself doesn't fully believe in herself.
Being of no attribute has always been a complex for her.
I nodded at May's words. She always showed a bright smile, but hidden behind that smile was a deep concern for Krush.
She had a broad perspective and was good at observing others.
"No attribute... I wish there was something I could do."
As I murmured this, May tugged at my sleeve with a small voice of joy.
"Lord Salt, please help Lady Krush! I believe you can be a great strength for her!"
Her words made me start to think about what I could do for her.
Because she had no attribute, the struggles she faced were deep.
But perhaps I could lighten that burden, even just a little.
As I watched Krush continue to fight alone, I quietly made a resolution in my heart.
After conducting Lady Rana's usual examination for her fear of men, and finishing our conversation, Krush came into the office.
"Krush?"
"Thank you for coming."
It seemed that Lady Rana had called for Krush.
"Excuse me! Lady Rana, Lord Salt."
"Um?"
"Lord Salt, I believe you will become an invaluable presence for the Fourth Knight Order from now on."
"Lady Rana."
I felt both moved by Lady Rana's words and bewildered that she thought so highly of me.
Therefore, I would like to assign Krush as your personal knight from now on.
She has wanted to repay the favor of being saved by you, Lord Salt.
Additionally, within the Fourth Knight Order, she is someone I trust alongside Freina.
Will you accept her strength and feelings?
Looking at Krush's face, I contemplated Lady Rana's words.
I didn't think I needed a bodyguard, but this was a kindness from both Lady Rana and Krush.
It wouldn't be right to refuse so easily.
"I understand. Thank you for considering it so deeply."
As I looked at Lady Rana, I could feel that she was gradually opening her heart to me.
Seeing her slowly overcoming her fear of men warmed my own heart.
In the following days, I spent more time with Lady Rana, but Krush was always there, accompanying us.
She quietly, yet resolutely, protected our backs.
And strangely enough, while Lady Rana showed embarrassment at actions I found embarrassing, Krush seemed unaffected.
"Krush, thank you as always. Even though you're my guard, I don't think there’s much danger here."
I lightly expressed my gratitude to Krush, who accompanied me even in the medical room and during Lady Rana's examinations.
Krush replied seriously, "This is my duty." Her earnest demeanor always impressed me.
At that moment, a request for investigation arrived from the Adventurers Guild for the Knight Order.
It was a request that had come because I was in the medical room as a helper for the Fourth Knight Order.
It seemed that the Adventurers Guild knew about my holy attribute.
The requester was the vice guild master of the Adventurers Guild, and I received an explanation from Lady Rana regarding the nomination.
It seems they want your help, Lord Salt.
Adventurers with holy attributes are extremely valuable, so the guild is expecting great things from you.
I see...
If it's a request from the Adventurers Guild, I have no reason to refuse.
After all, I am an adventurer.
I'll go to the guild and check the details.
"I will accompany you. As your personal knight, I will ensure your protection."
Krush and I left the Knight Order and headed for the Adventurers Guild.
It had been a while since I had come to the Adventurers Guild since arriving in Corias Territory.
As I opened the door to the Adventurers Guild, unlike the refined atmosphere of the royal capital, I was met with the rough gazes of the frontier's ruffians.
As I walked toward the reception, a trio of men stood up and approached us.
"Hey, hey, what’s the vice-captain of the female knight order doing here?"
"And bringing a man with her is rare, huh? Have you finally started using women instead of just swordsmanship?"
[img]https://i.imgur.com/KagR3Sx.jpeg
It seemed like the scum were making insinuations, surrounding Krush.
"This is a mission. Please leave us alone."
"Huh? Come on, we just got to the Adventurers Guild. How about pouring us a drink or something?"
"Yeah, yeah. You’re acting all high and mighty, but you can’t drink with us adventurers?"
"Or are you scared to be with that guy next to you? Hahaha!"
Seeing the men mock Krush, I decided I could no longer hold back.
As I stepped forward, Krush stopped me.
"Shut up, scum. I said I don't have time for you."
"Huh? Who are you calling scum?"
"Are you looking down on us? Do you think the Knight Order is impressive?"
"I never said that. I only deny you scum, not all adventurers."
"Huh!? Are you mocking us?!"
As one of the men lunged at her, Krush easily dodged and tripped him.
As expected of the vice-captain of the Fourth Knight Order. She was well-versed in combat.
However, the men seemed to have ulterior motives, and Krush was unaware of the fourth man sneaking up behind her with a club raised.
"Holy Impulse!"
I instantly unleashed a shockwave of holy attribute magic with my thumb, sending the man with the club crashing into the wall.
I followed up by sending the other three flying as I approached Krush.
"Lord Salt! I can handle this alone!"
"Well, I didn't want to escalate things too much. You know how it is when knights and adventurers clash."
"Ah!"
It seemed she understood what I was trying to say.
"I'm sorry."
"No, don't worry about it. The fault lies with them."
Had they intended to pick a fight with Krush and demand some kind of compensation?
Or were they targeting Krush herself?
There was no doubt they had mocked the Knight Order I belonged to.
Krush looked embarrassed, running her fingers through her beautiful silver hair.
If she stayed quiet, she would be beautiful, but perhaps she was being taught to act tough as a knight?
Krush seemed bewildered by being saved.
"What happened here?!"
As I pondered what to do now that I had taken down the adventurers, the receptionist of the Adventurers Guild approached.
A beautiful woman with reddish-brown hair tied up in a bun and glasses looked around the guild to assess the situation.
Other adventurers were watching us, but no one dared to approach.
"I'm sorry. It's just a little scuffle between adventurers."
"And you are?"
"I'm just a regular adventurer."
I showed my adventurer's card to prove my identity.
Upon seeing my adventurer's card, the receptionist looked surprised.
"Lord Salt of the Holy Light!"
Please stop! Don’t shout out that embarrassing title...
"Holy Light?"
Krush tilted her head behind me.
However, the Adventurers Guild began to buzz with excitement.
"Wait, seriously?!"
"Is that Holy Light?!"
"Whoa!? Here in this backwater?!"
I felt like sighing at the commotion in the Adventurers Guild.
Yes!
A healer who uses holy light and a dagger user.
The party of the famous A-rank adventurers, Lady Asha, the Sword Saint, and Lady Cynthia, the Precise Mage, is well-known even in the royal capital!
Don’t say everything!
Their achievements are significant, and I was just there for healing and reconnaissance.
It’s not something I want to boast about loudly.
"Is he really that amazing of an adventurer? So that’s how he was able to defeat the White King all by himself."
Krush, please stop saying unnecessary things right now! You know that creates misunderstandings, right?
Wow!
I’ve never heard that before!
The White King is said to be a type of calamity.
It’s said that even a group of A-rank adventurers would find it difficult to defeat one!
Why is she saying everything so loudly? Is it just me, or does it seem a bit theatrical?
"It was just a matter of compatibility."
Against the death attribute White King, I had the advantage due to my holy attribute.
"I see! That makes everything understandable. Lord Salt is indeed a necessary asset for the Knight Order!"
Please don’t look at me with those pure, sparkling eyes filled with respect.
Krush is straightforward in a good way, but too pure in a bad way. She probably doesn’t know how to be suspicious.
"More than anything, I’ve learned about Lord Salt’s unexpected background and title."
"I’m glad to learn about achievements I didn’t know about."
Why are the receptionist and Krush shaking hands?
I was astonished by their strange exchange when the adventurer I had knocked down stood up and asked.
"Uh, are you really Holy Light Salt?"
"I don’t like that title, but yes, it’s true."
"Y-You gotta forgive me! I just wanted to tease the Fourth Knight Order a bit since you guys showed up!"
"Ah! I’ll be purified and vanish!"
"We’re not some filthy spirits to be purified!"
The three of them screamed and backed away.
"Do adventurers have a bad relationship with the Fourth Knight Order?"
It’s not like that!
If you’re a man, you understand, right?
With all those beauties around, it’s only natural to want to get their attention!
I wasn’t pleased at all to be stared at with that lewd grin.
It’s true that Krush is a stunning beauty, Lady Rana has a voluptuous figure, and Freina and May are also beautiful or cute, making for a lineup of stunning women.
Usually, I tried not to think about their appearances from my position as their dedicated healer, but hearing it from another man made me realize it.
"I can understand that, but you should stop. I’ll be backing them up."
"Ugh! O-Okay. We’re not stupid enough to go against an A-rank."
With that, the three of them left.
In the countryside, there are inevitably more ruffians, making the security worse.
By the way, I wonder what the other adventurers think of me.
"Um, Lord Salt! What brings you here today?"
The receptionist's eyes sparkled as she directed a flirtatious gaze at me.
"I came to accept a nomination request from the Adventurers Guild."
"A nomination request?! I’ll look into that right away!"
After the receptionist checked, a meeting with the vice guild master was quickly arranged, and we were led to the vice guild master's room.
Welcome, Lord Salt.
I’m Lina Castor, the vice guild master of the Adventurers Guild.
I heard from the receptionist, Towa, that there was a bit of a scuffle, and I apologize as the administrator.
"No, I’m glad it didn’t escalate. I don’t mind."
I’m relieved to hear that.
Adventurers with holy attributes are extremely rare.
The guild values your abilities, so we wanted you to accept this request.
Inside the room was the vice guild master of the Adventurers Guild.
She welcomed us with sharp eyes and a calm demeanor, smiling at me.
"So, what’s the request today?"
Lina's expression turned a bit serious as she spread out some documents.
Actually, there have been strange phenomena occurring near Corias Territory.
Miasma is spreading rapidly, and in some villages, the residents are falling ill.
It’s believed that this is not a normal illness but likely the influence of monsters.
With your holy attribute, we hope you can help identify the cause and purify the miasma.
Miasma... again. The cause of Lady Rana's previous illness was also miasma.
Last time, it developed into cursed poison, but I hoped it wouldn't be that severe this time.
"I intend to take on that investigation. Krush, will you accompany me?"
"Of course, Lord Salt. I will protect you."
Lina nodded in satisfaction at that.
"Thank you, that’s a good answer. I’m counting on your investigation and report. Please be careful."
We nodded at the vice guild master's words and left the Adventurers Guild.
Returning to the Knight Order and entering Lady Rana's office, she was facing her desk as usual.
Noticing my presence, Lady Rana looked up with a gentle smile.
"Welcome back, Lord Salt. Could you give me a report on your time at the Adventurers Guild?"
Yes, Lady Rana.
I received an investigation request from the Adventurers Guild.
It seems there has been a sharp increase in villagers complaining of illness in the frontier villages.
I was told that miasma is likely involved.
I sat close to Lady Rana. As part of her treatment for her fear of men, I tried to sit as close to her as possible.
I felt her hand tremble slightly, but it wasn't as tense as before.
Previously, even this distance seemed difficult for her, but now she was gradually showing signs of calm.
"So, you’re going to that village."
Yes.
I’ll be heading out with Krush for the investigation.
However, I might be away for a while.
That’s why I came back to ask for your permission.
Krush is likely getting permission from Lady Freina right now.
"I see. Of course, I give you my permission. Please do your best for the people of the territory."
"Yes! Of course."
Lady Rana gently took my hand. From her hand, I felt warmth and the concern that she was worried about my trembling.
"I may not be able to return until the investigation is over, but I will do my best to come back as soon as possible."
For a moment, Lady Rana looked down, appearing lonely, but she quickly smiled and gazed at me.
"That’s alright. I believe that Lord Salt will definitely return safely. Please take care."
Feeling the warmth of her hand, I nodded.
In this moment of stillness, I could sense how her fear of men was gradually healing.
I also realized how significant my role was for her.
"Thank you. It gives me strength to hear you say that, Lady Rana."
I gently released her hand and stood up.
Lady Rana wore a slightly reluctant expression, but she quickly returned a soft smile.
"Be careful, Lord Salt."
I bowed and left Lady Rana's office.
Krush and I, swaying on horseback, took two or three days to finally arrive at the village afflicted by illness, far from the capital of Corias.
During the journey, I felt uneasy about the vast wilderness and rocky landscapes, but more than that, I was worried about the illness spreading in the village.
